comments.value:
These are the changes I foresee needed to make this work:
- Update the avatar SDK and add a dropdown to the Pipeline Manager script that lets you select which layer this GameObject belongs to
- Update the backend to store this info and link layers together based on the Blueprint ID
- Update the game client to submit the user's performance preference with the avatar request when loading someone's avatar
- Update the backend to send the correct .vrca file for the user's preference from the previous list item
- Update the game client to let users select all performance ranks as their preferred setting as opposed to vpoor, poor, and medium only

Hmmm I like the *idea*, but... most avatar creators aren't even willing to optimize their avatar above *very poor*, right?
This seems like a very complex system few avatar creators would use. And those who would are already skilled enough to optimize an avatar & make it look good.
This would also further increase the discrepancy between PCVR / Quest / Fallback avatars.
The avatar performance ranking system isn't perfect though, and I'm sure it could be improved.

@{5f8a26770aaa28611fedd6b6|full_name}: I wouldn't say it's complex, it's basically the equivalent of having more fallback slots, but I see what you mean. I think the people this would be most useful to is the core community and people who make avatars for themselves.
I got this idea after I made like 4 separate avatars that are essentially the same but have different performance ranks. Doing this idea would clear up the "my avatars" section a lot.

@{5f3736ad3c4bc468c92c522f|full_name}: Even if they would implement that, just like @{5f8a26770aaa28611fedd6b6|full_name} is dont see a lot of people using it. If you purely look at downloadsizes of a lot of avatars, you will notice that majority dont even give two thoughts about what texture size is. 
And this is where the problems with the current performance rank system begin, it is simply i would say... "outdated" and does not take a lot of what we learned and how avatars changed over the years into consideration.
1. why 70.001 polys as very poor, when a 140.000 avatar can outperform 70.000 ones when the skinned mesh renderes are done properly? (They dont take shapekeys into consideration, which cause calculations over the whole skinned mesh renderer)
2. vram usage is not considered - thats a newer thing, especially with the higher quality of avatars we began to see this year. There is no difference in performance ranking if you would use 400MB of vram or 33MB (which is a huge difference). Especially in vr one sees the stuttering whenever you turn around in a full lobby and have to load 2-3 such nukes in.
---
overall, i like your idea as well, but before they readdress the performance ranking system in general (those two points are examples, i think there may be even more, but i am not a developer after all) sticking with the current system is their best shot for now.

details:
Now that we have had some time to get used to the fallback system on stable, I want to strongly recommend extending this feature with layers. Based on the current stable branch, this feels like not that much development work.
I'm using some new terminology here, where layers are different fallbacks incuded with avatars.
In this new system, avatar authors would be able to upload up to 10 layers (2 for each performance rank) of the same avatar, with decreasing levels of detail/feature set.
The avatar authoring workflow for example would thus be as follows:
- Create the initial base, with an unlimited number of tris (for posing and rendering in the modeler, or any other non-VRChat use)
- Decimate for very poor/poor rank, add heavy features in Unity. Put this in layer 0.
- Decimate and optimise for medium rank, add less features. Put this in layer 1.
- Decimate and optimise for good rank, add small features. Put this in layer 2.
This would result in 3 layers, uploaded into the same blueprint ID. When done, players would be able to set their preferred performance settings in the safety menu just like now, except the options would extend up to very good instead of stopping at medium.
When loading an avatar, the game would select the layer closest to the user's preference by matching upwards. For example, if I selected "poor" in this new imaginary Safety setting, the game would display layers marked as "poor" and better, preferring the worse performance ones, which is "poor" as I chose that. If an avatar doesn't have that exact quality available, it would look for "medium" next, and so on.
If an avatar doesn't have a layer applicable for the player's settings, the current behaviour would continue as normal and display the user's chosen fallback, or the grey robot if the chosen fallback avatar also doesn't have a matching layer.
I think this mechanism is more robust than just having users select avatars as fallback, and give avatar creators a way better chance to showcase their creativity. It's also better for non-creators, as they'd be able to see more of the diverse avatars we have.
To recap:
Avatar authors should be able to upload avatars with an LOD-like system, and users should be able to choose their preferred setting.
Expansion:
The game could use these layers for actual LOD behaviour and switch between layers depending on distance.
title: Avatar performance layers
